subject: Clarify SOC 2 report boundary: partial month inclusion and bridge letter
messages:
From: Elaine Porter <elaine@bluewavehealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: security@bluewavehealth.com
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — report end date vs. month inclusion

Dylan —

Thanks again for sending over the SOC 2 Type II report. One quick clarification from our audit team: the report we received lists the period ending 28 Feb 2027. Are the calendar months up to and including February considered "in scope" (i.e., full-month coverage through 2/28), or is the report considered a point-in-time cutoff and we should treat February as a partial month?

Related: we need to confirm whether configuration snapshots for logging and retention that the auditors may request would reflect the state on 2027-02-28 23:59 UTC, or if we should expect differences for any reasons after that timestamp. If the latter is the case, can Redwood provide a bridge letter or attestation that controls remained materially unchanged between 2/28/2027 and the date the evidence is exported?

I've attached our requested evidence checklist for context.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Porter
Director, Information Security
BlueWave Health

Are the calendar months up to and including February considered "in scope" (i.e., full-month coverage through 2/28), or is the report considered a point-in-time cutoff and we should treat February as a partial month?
>

If the latter is the case, can Redwood provide a bridge letter or attestation that controls remained materially unchanged between 2/28/2027 and the date the evidence is exported?

Short answer: the Type II report covers continuous testing for the period 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28 (inclusive). For audit purposes, that means the controls were evaluated across that range — February 2027 is included as part of the reporting period rather than a single point-in-time snapshot.

That said, auditors frequently request point-in-time artifacts (configuration exports, log extracts) aligned to a specific timestamp. We can provide: 1) configuration snapshots taken at 2027-02-28 23:59:00 UTC where available, and 2) a signed bridge letter/attestation confirming that there were no material changes to the described control environment between 2027-02-28 and the date of evidence export.

I've looped in Irene (security operations) and Rishi (compliance) to confirm what artifacts we can produce and the expected turnaround. I'm attaching a generic bridge-letter template we use — we'll tailor it and sign it once you confirm the exact controls and environment you need evidence for.

Next steps for us:
- Confirm which systems/environments you need point-in-time evidence for (e.g., prod-us-east-1).
- Confirm which controls on your checklist are highest priority (e.g., logging retention, data deletion, change control).
- We'll pull the 2/28 snapshots and prepare the attestation; expected lead time 1–3 business days depending on scope.

If you can reply with the bullet list of items and environments, we'll start pulling artifacts.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Customer Security Manager
Redwood Inference
